item.title: Congress Targets D.C. Tax Authority as Trump Law Drives Deficit Surge
item.description: The Tax Foundation has warned that President Trump's One Big Beautiful Bill Act will result in increased federal deficits and decreased local revenue for Washington, D.C., if Congress overrides the city's decision to decouple from the federal tax law. The post Congress Targets D.C. Tax Authority as Trump Law Drives Deficit Surge appeared first on The Washington Informer.

item.title: Comfort Over Chaos: Inside the New Self-Care Choices Women and Men Are Making
item.description: Women are prioritizing rest and connection with close friends, while men are investing more time and money in grooming routines, both shifts reflecting a cultural recalibration towards intention and self-awareness. The post Comfort Over Chaos: Inside the New Self-Care Choices Women and Men Are Making appeared first on The Washington Informer.

item.title: Alzheimer’s Cases Climb Among Black and Latino Americans as New Campaign Promotes Early Screening
item.description: AlzInColor is a campaign aimed at raising awareness and promoting early detection of Alzheimer's disease in Black and Latino communities, which are disproportionately affected by the disease. The post Alzheimer’s Cases Climb Among Black and Latino Americans as New Campaign Promotes Early Screening appeared first on The Washington Informer.

item.title: Rock & Roll Hall of Fame Fight Flares Again as Gene Simmons Targets Rap Inductions
item.description: Gene Simmons has sparked controversy by questioning why hip-hop artists are inducted into the Rock & Roll Hall of Fame, citing the absence of bands such as Iron Maiden as evidence that the institution has strayed from its name. The post Rock & Roll Hall of Fame Fight Flares Again as Gene Simmons Targets Rap Inductions appeared first on The Washington Informer.

item.title: Schwalb Targets Alleged Slumlord Network in First-of-Its-Kind Racketeering Lawsuit
item.description: The District of Columbia filed a lawsuit against Ali "Sam" Razjooyan, his brother Eimon "Ray" Razjooyan, and their mother Houri Razjooyan for allegedly operating a decade-long real estate fraud enterprise that left hundreds of tenants living in hazardous conditions while siphoning tens of millions of dollars from lenders and city housing programs. The post Schwalb Targets Alleged Slumlord Network in First-of-Its-Kind Racketeering Lawsuit appeared first on The Washington Informer.

item.title: SMITH: Locked Out of the Game — Why Access to Sports Media Matters to Local Communities
item.description: The Washington Post's recent decision to lay off hundreds of employees and eliminate its entire sports department has sparked a debate about the importance of local sports coverage and the need for accessible sports content for fans. The post SMITH: Locked Out of the Game — Why Access to Sports Media Matters to Local Communities appeared first on The Washington Informer.

item.title: Maryland Federal Leaders Sponsor Bill to Protect Black History
item.description: Sen. Angela Alsobrooks (D-Md.) and Rep. Kweisi Mfume (D-Md.) are sponsoring the National Council on African American History and Culture Act to establish a 12-member advisory council within the National Endowment for the Humanities to preserve and promote African American history and culture. The post Maryland Federal Leaders Sponsor Bill to Protect Black History appeared first on The Washington Informer.

item.title: Alsobrooks Sponsors Bill to Examine Fiscal Effects of Federal Mass Firings
item.description: Maryland Democratic Sen. Angela Alsobrooks has sponsored the Fiscal Harms of Federal Firings Act, which would direct the Government Accountability Office to conduct a comprehensive study of the financial effects of the Trump administration's mass firings on state and local governments. The post Alsobrooks Sponsors Bill to Examine Fiscal Effects of Federal Mass Firings appeared first on The Washington Informer.

item.title: Don Lemon Enters Not Guilty Plea in Minnesota Church Protest Case
item.description: Don Lemon, a former CNN anchor, pleaded not guilty to charges of interfering with access to a house of worship and conspiring against the rights of religious freedom at a January protest inside Cities Church, while insisting that the First Amendment protects his right to report the news. The post Don Lemon Enters Not Guilty Plea in Minnesota Church Protest Case appeared first on The Washington Informer.

item.title: Wizards NBA All-Star Friday Night Preview: Bub Carrington to Replace Alex Sarr In Rising Stars Game
item.description: The Washington Wizards will be represented by three players in the 2026 NBA All-Star Weekend Rising Stars Challenge, showcasing the team's bright young core and signaling a promising future for the franchise.
